- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent high or use 20-day moving average for smoothing.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days falling >2% from peak), model overreacts; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day of reversion.
- When sentiment is positive but price declines, model may lag; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in true trend reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply 1–2% downward correction for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.37, -0.53, +0.37), model tends to misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days for trend correction.
